description: Exclusion-set field matching is top-level only: an excluded name occurring again inside a nested object is NOT stripped. Pins the current canonical_digest() behavior (lib/cpb/canonicalize.py) so a recursive-stripping implementation forks on this vector. Falsification test proposed by Anton Sokolov in PR #2 review; see issue for the interop-fork risk this closes.
spec_ref: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §4 ('exclusion set ... matched against the top-level member names of the payload only')
note: The top-level 'id' is stripped; the nested 'sub.id' survives because exclusion-set matching does not recurse. A recursive-stripping implementation would also remove sub.id, leaving sub={} which normalization then removes entirely, producing sha256("{}") = 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a instead -- a digest fork on any payload nesting an excluded field name (e.g. a chain field that plausibly nests).
